title: dotfiles-managed keyboard remaps
_notes: Source of truth for every Karabiner rule this repo owns. Edit this file,
then run ./install.sh (or generate.py alone to refresh rules/managed.json).
Never hand-edit rules/managed.json - it is generated.
Never hand-edit ~/.config/karabiner/karabiner.json for anything defined
here; the next install.sh run replaces it.
prefix: every generated rule description starts with this. install.sh
deletes all rules with this prefix before appending the current set, which
is what makes re-running replace rather than duplicate, and what makes
deleting a group here actually remove it. Rules you add by hand in the
Karabiner GUI have no prefix and are left alone.
scopes: named condition blocks referenced by each group's `scope`.
mode 'if'        = fire ONLY in the listed apps (allowlist)
mode 'unless'    = fire EVERYWHERE EXCEPT the listed apps (denylist)
mode 'device_if' = fire only for events from the listed keyboards, which
takes `identifiers` (vendor_id/product_id) rather than
`bundle_identifiers`. Get the numbers from:
karabiner_cli --list-connected-devices
null             = no condition at all, fires everywhere
Scoping cannot see inside an app: tmux inside Alacritty reads as Alacritty
(good), and VS Code's integrated terminal reads as VS Code (less good - the
letter remaps do apply in that pane).
Find a bundle id with: osascript -e 'id of app "AppName"'
or use Karabiner-EventViewer > Frontmost Application tab.
Deliberately NOT mapped, because something else already owns the chord:
ctrl+shift+r  -> vscode/keybindings.json runs all notebook cells
Adding `optional: ["shift"]` to r would swallow that before VS Code sees
it. Karabiner runs BEFORE aerospace and before any app, so a chord mapped
here never reaches whatever else wanted it.
ctrl+k and ctrl+period exist so the claude.ai web app's chat search and
sidebar toggle work from a PC chord. Both are also useful in VS Code, where
cmd+k is the chord prefix and cmd+period is Quick Fix, matching what ctrl+k
and ctrl+period do there on Windows. ctrl+k is safe despite being kill-line
in a shell, because the gui scope excludes terminals, and it does not touch
aerospace's alt-ctrl-k resize binding, which needs alt as well.
`e` is the odd one out: it takes shift as MANDATORY, not optional, so only
ctrl+shift+e is mapped and plain ctrl+e is left alone. ctrl+shift+e is the
VS Code explorer, but plain cmd+e in Finder is EJECT, and a stray ctrl+e
unmounting a disk is a worse failure than a missing shortcut.
Three chords were freed by moving the aerospace binding that held them,
because the VS Code meaning is worth more than a launcher on a chord no
other platform uses for that:
ctrl+shift+p -> command palette   (incognito moved to alt-i)
ctrl+shift+d -> Run and Debug     (drag cancel moved to alt-shift-c)
ctrl+shift+x -> Extensions        (dismiss notifs moved to alt-shift-x)
`d` takes shift as mandatory so plain ctrl+d stays the browsers-only
bookmark mapping.
Three mappings emit a DIFFERENT key than they receive, because the Windows
chord and the macOS chord disagree on the letter:
ctrl+y -> cmd+shift+z   Windows redo. macOS cmd+y is History, not redo.
ctrl+h -> cmd+y         Windows history. macOS cmd+h HIDES the app.
ctrl+j -> cmd+shift+j   Windows downloads. Plain cmd+j is nothing useful.
ctrl+shift+r is in the browsers scope, not gui, on purpose: it is hard
reload in a browser but vscode/keybindings.json wants it for notebooks. The
gui `r` mapping has no optional shift, so ctrl+shift+r falls through the gui
rule and only the browsers rule catches it. Same trick keeps ctrl+shift+i
and ctrl+shift+delete browser-only while plain ctrl+i is italic and plain
ctrl+backspace is delete-word.
The Glove80 group makes its Super-position key drive AeroSpace, the way
the Windows key drives i3 on Arch. AeroSpace's mod is `alt`, so Command
has to become Option on that keyboard. It is a SWAP, not a one-way map:
a one-way map would leave the Glove80 with no Command key at all, killing
cmd+space, cmd+tab and cmd+q from it. Both sides are swapped because the
board's layout is non-standard (its Ctrl reports as right_control), so
which side the Super key uses is not worth assuming.
`optional: ["any"]` on those four is load-bearing, not decoration. Without
it the modifier only matches when nothing else is held, which breaks every
Super+Shift chord: aerospace's move-window and move-to-workspace bindings.
Fixing this in the Glove80's ZMK firmware instead would break i3 on Arch,
which wants that same physical key to stay Super. Karabiner is per-machine,
so the keyboard keeps sending Super and only macOS reinterprets it.
Word navigation and delete-word are in the gui scope, NOT everywhere. They
used to be everywhere, on the theory that Option+Arrow and Option+Backspace
are useful in a shell. They are not, in this terminal: Alacritty defaults
option_as_alt to None on macOS, so Option+Arrow arrives as a bare arrow and
Option+Backspace as a bare delete. Worse, the rewrite was stealing chords
the terminal already handles correctly on its own. Excluded from terminals,
the native path works end to end:
ctrl+arrow     -> alacritty sends ^[[1;5C/D, oh-my-zsh binds both
ctrl+delete    -> alacritty sends ^[[3;5~, oh-my-zsh binds it to kill-word
ctrl+backspace -> alacritty.toml sends ^W (terminals cannot tell it from a
plain backspace, so it needs the explicit binding)
^W is also what makes this work inside tmux: tmux's command-prompt binds C-w
to delete-word, and binds Meta-Backspace to nothing at all (measured), so a
rename-window prompt only deletes a word if ^W is what reaches it.

groups.description: Glove80 only: swap Command and Option
Glove80 in browsers: give the Alt key back its Option chords
Ctrl+Backspace/Delete deletes a word (not in terminals)
Browser chords: address bar, bookmarks, history, downloads, devtools, source
